question_text: Compare I2C and SPI in terms of speed, pin count, and communication type (duplex).
answer_text: SPI is much faster and full-duplex but requires more pins. I2C is slower and half-duplex but uses only two pins for any number of devices.
explanation_text:
Speed: SPI frequently hits 10+ MHz. I2C is usually 100 kHz (Standard), 400 kHz (Fast), or 1 MHz (Fast+).
Duplex: SPI is full-duplex (can send and receive at the exact same time via separate MOSI and MISO lines). I2C is half-duplex (SDA is shared, so it can only send OR receive at one time).
Pins: I2C always uses 2 shared pins (SDA, SCL). SPI uses 3 shared pins (SCLK, MOSI, MISO) plus 1 dedicated CS pin per slave.
bonus_question_text: Which protocol has built-in hardware acknowledgment to verify the device actually received the data?
bonus_answer_text: I2C. The receiving device must pull the SDA line low (ACK) after every byte. SPI has no hardware acknowledgment; the master blindly clocks out data.
